source_record.native_common_basis: Keep release readiness visible while separating integration, deployment and authorized exposure decisions.
common_cost_and_alternative: Account for structural work, requalification, telemetry, isolation, rehearsal, backup, coexistence, maintenance and delayed beneficial change; do not count the same shared capacity twice.

Two bounded practitioner-source accesses corroborate mechanisms, not universal causal effects. No deployed experiment, new property, whole synthesis completion or independent acceptance.

positive_controls.argument: Architectural interface and resource constraints specify which candidate evidence matters and which superficially deployable package is unsuitable for the intended system.
The applicable envelope, evidence validity and change-trigger rules determine which qualification conditions must be satisfied before the candidate may be called ready for that use.
Hazard-control requirements and actual risk-acceptance authority define the consequence-sensitive release conditions and prevent automatic exposure merely because the candidate builds.
Actual transition conditions and delegated authority determine when and where the prepared candidate may be exposed, and which operational deficits remain despite technical success.
Recovery and compatibility tests constrain what a candidate must preserve and whether its deployment can truthfully claim a usable rollback or containment path.
Support horizon, fielded versions and retirement obligations identify which candidate lines must remain maintainable and which can deliberately be ended.
Actual consequences, recovery limits, coupling and obligations determine the appropriate candidate evidence and exposure authorization without prescribing a universal deployment frequency.
Rejecting the universal phase curve removes a false requirement to freeze all future candidate changes early and demands actual evidence for batching or extra control.
